facts.statement: Dakotaraptor lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Maastrichtian age.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian),

facts.statement: The genus Dakotaraptor was described by DePalma and colleagues in 2015.
facts.quote: authority: DePalma et al. 2015

facts.statement: The type species of the genus is Dakotaraptor steini.
facts.quote: type_species: Dakotaraptor steini

facts.statement: Remains found in the Maastrichtian-aged Hell Creek Formation suggest Dakotaraptor was potentially one of the last surviving dromaeosaurids, a classification disputed by other researchers.
facts.quote: The remains have been found in the Maastrichtian-aged Hell Creek Formation, dated to the very end of the Mesozoic era, making Dakotaraptor potentially one of the last surviving dromaeosaurids, though other researchers have disputed its classification.

facts.statement: Dakotaraptor was one of the largest dromaeosaurids, with estimates of 4.35 to 6 meters in length and 220 to 350 kilograms in weight.
facts.quote: One of the largest dromaeosaurids, measuring 4.35 - 6 m and weighing 220 - 350 kg, the remains of D. steini were discovered in a multi-species bonebed.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Robert DePalma discovered the site yielding Dakotaraptor remains in Harding County, South Dakota, in 2005.
facts.quote: In 2005, paleontologist Robert DePalma in Harding County, South Dakota discovered a fluvial bonebed bearing the remains of a variety of dinosaurian and non-dinosaurian remains, which yielded a partial skeleton attributed by DePalma to a large dromaeosaurid.

facts.statement: The species Dakotaraptor steini was formally named and described in 2015 by DePalma, Burnham, Martin, Larson, and Bakker.
facts.quote: In 2015, the type species Dakotaraptor steini was named and described by Robert A. DePalma, David A. Burnham, Larry Dean Martin, Peter Lars Larson, and Robert Thomas Bakker.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was found in the upper Hell Creek Formation, dating to the late Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: The holotype, PBMNH.P.10.113.T, was found in a sandstone layer of the upper Hell Creek Formation, dating to the late Maastrichtian.

facts.statement: By 2024, some dinosaurian elements of Dakotaraptor were questioned, as traits thought diagnostic for dromaeosaurs were also found in caenagnathids and ornithomimosaurians.
facts.quote: In 2024, even the dinosaurian elements of Dakotaraptor were questioned, with supposed traits diagnostic for dromaeosaurs also referrable to caenagnathids and ornithomimosaurians.

facts.statement: The prominent bumps on the ulna are called ulnar papillae or quill knobs, which served as attachment points for wing feathers.
facts.quote: These are called ulnar papillae, more commonly known as quill knobs. In birds and some other theropod dinosaurs, these bumps were spots for reinforced attachment of the remiges, or wing feathers.

facts.statement: The estimated wingspan of Dakotaraptor is 120 cm, excluding possible primary feathers longer than the hand.
facts.quote: The wingspan of Dakotaraptor was estimated at 120 cm, not taking into account possible primary remiges longer than the hand.

facts.statement: The first Dakotaraptor fossils were found in South Dakota, USA, in 2005.
facts.quote: Los primeros fósiles de Dakotaraptor fueron hallados en Dakota del Sur, Estados Unidos en 2005.

facts.statement: The genus Dakotaraptor, meaning "Dakota thief", was named in 2015 upon the description of its type species Dakotaraptor steini.
facts.quote: En 2015, se nombró al género Dakotaraptor, que significa "ladrón de Dakota", en la descripción de su especie tipo Dakotaraptor steini.

facts.statement: Dakotaraptor measured between five and six meters in length, making it one of the largest known dromaeosaurids alongside Utahraptor, Austroraptor, and Achillobator.
facts.quote: Dakotaraptor medía entre cinco a seis metros de longitud, lo cual lo convierte en uno de los mayores dromeosáuridos conocidos junto con el norteamericano Utahraptor, el suramericano Austroraptor, y el asiático Achillobator.

facts.statement: Dakotaraptor had long arms, and a forearm bone shows quill knobs that confirm it was feathered.
facts.quote: Tenía brazos largos. Uno de los huesos del antebrazo muestra protuberancias para las plumas, lo que confirma que Dakotaraptor estaba emplumado.

facts.statement: Dakotaraptor possessed long legs with a highly developed claw on the second toe.
facts.quote: Poseía patas largas con una garra muy desarrollada en el segundo dedo del pie.

facts.statement: Dakotaraptor is exceptionally large for a dromaeosaurid, with an estimated adult length of 5.5 meters.
facts.quote: Dakotaraptor es excepcionalmente grande para un dromeosáurido; se estima que la longitud de un adulto sería de 5.5 metros.

facts.statement: The length of the Dakotaraptor thighbone is 558 mm.
facts.quote: The length of the thighbone is 558 mm.

facts.statement: The holotype shinbone is 678 mm long, making it the longest dromaeosaurid tibia known.
facts.quote: The holotype shinbone is, with a length of 678 mm, the longest dromaeosaurid tibia known.

facts.statement: It cannot yet be deduced which morph was male and which was female.
facts.quote: It can as yet not be deduced which morph was male and which morph was female.

facts.statement: Adult Dakotaraptor individuals were too heavy to fly, yet their feathers were not reduced despite this flightless condition.
facts.quote: Adult Dakotaraptor individuals were much too heavy to fly. Despite this flightless condition, the feathers were not reduced.

facts.statement: Dakotaraptor was placed in Dromaeosauridae, and a cladistic analysis showed it was the sister taxon of Dromaeosaurus.
facts.quote: Dakotaraptor was placed in Dromaeosauridae. A cladistic analysis showed that it was the sister taxa of Dromaeosaurus.

facts.statement: A 2019 study by Hartman et al. recovered a placement of Dakotaraptor in Unenlagiidae.
facts.quote: A recent study conducted by Hartman et al. 2019 recovered a placement of Dakotaraptor in Unenlagiidae.

facts.statement: The genus authority for Dakotaraptor is DePalma et al., 2015.
facts.quote: genus_authority: DePalma et al., 2015

facts.statement: The species authority for Dakotaraptor steini is DePalma et al., 2015.
facts.quote: species_authority: DePalma et al., 2015

facts.statement: Dakotaraptor had a reduced protuberance for the flexor tendon attachment on the fourth toe claw.
facts.quote: En la cuarta garra del pie, la protuberancia que servía como sujeción para el tendón del músculo flexor es de tamaño reducido.

facts.statement: The blood groove on the outer face of the fourth toe claw was completely closed for nearly half its length, forming a tubular bone structure.
facts.quote: El "surco de sangre" en la cara externa de la cuarta garra del pie queda totalmente cerrado en cerca de la mitad de su longitud, formando una estructura ósea tubular.

facts.statement: The second and third toe claws possessed sharp keels on their lower zones.
facts.quote: La segunda y tercera garras del pie tienen quillas afiladas en sus zonas inferiores.

facts.statement: The second toe claw, known as the "killer claw," measured 29% of the femur length.
facts.quote: La segunda garra del pie, la "garra asesina", tiene una longitud equivalente al 29% de la longitud del fémur.

facts.statement: The fibular crest on the tibia was long and light in constitution, with a height not exceeding 9% of the crest length.
facts.quote: En la tibia, la crista fibularis, la cresta que hace contacto con el peroné, es larga y de constitución ligera con una altura que no excede el 9% de la longitud de la cresta.

facts.statement: The upper edge of the fibular crest ended in a hook.
facts.quote: El borde superior de esta cresta termina en un gancho.

facts.statement: On the second metacarpal, the inner condyle contacting the digit was nearly as large as the outer one.
facts.quote: En el segundo metacarpiano, de los dos cóndilos que hacen contacto con el dedo, el interior es casi tan grande como el externo.

facts.statement: The back vertebrae were highly pneumatized, filled with trabecular bone containing many air spaces.
facts.quote: Las vértebras de la espalda estaban sumamente neumatizadas, llenas de hueso trabecular que tiene muchos espacios con aire.

facts.statement: These elongated processes made the tail rigid.
facts.quote: Esto hacía rígida la cola.

facts.statement: Dakotaraptor likely had a furcula shaped between a U and V, similar to many dromaeosaurids like Velociraptor and the large spinosaurid Suchomimus.
facts.quote: Dakotaraptor tendría una fúrcula con una forma entre la de una U a V, similar a la de muchos otros dromeosáuridos como Velociraptor, e incluso el gran terópodo espinosáurido Suchomimus.

facts.statement: In 2015, researchers suggested that the alleged furculae of Dakotaraptor actually represented part of a turtle shell, specifically the entoplastron of Axestemys splendida.
facts.quote: En 2015, un estudio realizado por Victoria Megan Arbour y colaboradores se afirmó que las presuntas fúrculas de Dakotaraptor de hecho representaban parte de un caparazón de tortuga, más específicamente el entoplastrón de Axestemys splendida, un miembro de la familia Trionychidae.

facts.statement: In 2016, DePalma et al. recognized that none of the referred furculae actually belonged to Dakotaraptor and excluded them from the material.
facts.quote: En 2016, DePalma et al. reconoció que ninguna de las fúrculas referidas en realidad pertenecía a Dakotaraptor, y las excluyó del material referido.

facts.statement: The humerus, the upper arm bone, was relatively long and slender, and slightly curved inward.
facts.quote: El húmero, el hueso superior del brazo, es relativamente largo y delgado, y algo curvado hacia adentro.

facts.statement: The most notable anatomical feature was a row of protuberances along a crest on the lower edge of the ulna, known as ulnar papillae.
facts.quote: La característica anatómica más notable es la fila de protuberancias a lo largo de una cresta en el borde inferior de la ulna, uno de los huesos del antebrazo. Estas son conocidas como papilas ulnares.

facts.statement: The complete set is estimated to have included up to fifteen of these ulnar papillae.
facts.quote: Se estima que el conjunto completo podría incluir a quince de estas papilas ulnares.

facts.statement: The wingspan of Dakotaraptor was estimated at 120 centimeters, not counting possible primary flight feathers that would be longer than the hand.
facts.quote: La envergadura de Dakotaraptor se estimó en 120 centímetros, sin tomar en cuenta las posibles rémiges primarias que serían más largas que la mano.

facts.statement: The second metacarpal, the bone to which primary flight feathers were attached, also had a flattened bony lamina on its dorsal surface.
facts.quote: El segundo metacarpiano de los metacarpos de la mano, el hueso al que se sujetaban las rémiges primarias, también tenía una lámina ósea aplanada en su superficie dorsal.

facts.statement: Generally, the hind limbs were of light constitution with long bone elements, unlike the robust limbs of Utahraptor.
facts.quote: En general, los miembros posteriores eran de constitución ligera y con elementos óseos largos, al contrario de las robustas extremidades de Utahraptor.

facts.statement: The femur had a length of 558 millimeters.
facts.quote: El fémur tiene una longitud de 558 milímetros.

facts.statement: The tibia of the holotype has a length of 678 millimeters, being the largest among dromaeosaurids.
facts.quote: La tibia del holotipo tiene una longitud de 678 milímetros, siendo la de mayor tamaño entre los dromeosáuridos.

facts.statement: The tibia is 22% longer than the femur, indicating good running ability.
facts.quote: Es 22% más larga que el fémur, indicando una buena capacidad corredora.

facts.statement: The cnemial crest of the tibia has a sharp corner pointing forward.
facts.quote: La cresta cnemial de la tibia tiene una esquina afilada apuntando al frente.

facts.statement: Its fibular crest ends in a hook-shaped process pointing upward, a condition unique among all Theropods.
facts.quote: Su cresta fibular termina en un proceso en forma de gancho apuntando hacia arriba, una condición única entre todos los Theropoda.

facts.statement: The foot claws of Dakotaraptor include the typical elongated second claw of dromaeosaurids, or "killer claw," which was used to restrain or kill prey.
facts.quote: Las garras del pie de Dakotaraptor incluyen la típica segunda garra alargada de los dromeosáuridos, o "garra asesina", la cual era usada para restringir o matar a sus presas.

facts.statement: Dakotaraptor had a larger flexor tubercle relative to the total size of its claw than other discovered dromaeosaurids, potentially giving it the greatest cutting force of any known member of this group.
facts.quote: Dakotaraptor tenía un tubérculo flexor más grande en relación con el tamaño total de su garra que el de otros dromeosáuridos descubiertos, dándole potencialmente la mayor fuerza de corte de cualquier miembro conocido de este grupo.

facts.statement: The flexor tubercle on the third toe claw is almost non-existent, very reduced in size compared to other dromaeosaurids, suggesting more limited use of that claw.
facts.quote: El tubérculo flexor en la tercera garra del pie es casi inexistente, muy reducido en tamaño en comparación con otros dromeosáuridos, lo que sugiere un uso más limitado de esa garra.

facts.statement: The groove on its outer face ends in a bony tunnel directed toward the tip, a rare condition.
facts.quote: El surco en su cara externa termina en un túnel óseo en dirección a la punta, una condición rara.

facts.statement: Robert DePalma discovered the skeleton of a large dromaeosaurid in Harding County, South Dakota, in 2005.
facts.quote: En 2005, el paleontólogo Robert DePalma descubrió el esqueleto de un gran dromeosáurido en el condado de Harding, en Dakota del Sur.

facts.statement: The species Dakotaraptor steini was named and described in 2015 by Robert A. DePalma, David A. Burnham, Larry Dean Martin, Peter Lars Larson, and Robert Thomas Bakker.
facts.quote: En 2015, la especie tipo Dakotaraptor steini fue nombrada y descrita por Robert A. DePalma, David A. Burnham, Larry Dean Martin, Peter Lars Larson y Robert Thomas Bakker.

facts.statement: The genus name combines a reference to South Dakota and the Dakota people with the Latin term raptor, meaning "thief".
facts.quote: El nombre del género combina la referencia a Dakota del Sur y al pueblo dakota con el término en latín raptor, "ladrón".

facts.statement: The species name honors the paleontologist Walter W. Stein.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie homenajea al paleontólogo Walter W. Stein.

facts.statement: The holotype was found in sandstone layers from the upper part of the Hell Creek Formation, dating to the late Maastrichtian.
facts.quote: El holotipo, PBMNH.P.10.113.T, fue hallado en una capa de arenisca de la zona superior de la Formación Hell Creek, que data de finales del Maastrichtiense.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial adult skeleton lacking a skull.
facts.quote: Consiste de un esqueleto parcial que carece del cráneo, de un individuo adulto.

facts.statement: Additional fossils found at the site belong to a more gracile morph of Dakotaraptor.
facts.quote: Aparte de los restos del holotipo, en el sitio se descubrieron huesos que también pertenecieron a Dakotaraptor pero que representan un morfo más grácil.

facts.statement: Dakotaraptor is classified within the family Dromaeosauridae.
facts.quote: Dakotaraptor fue situado en la familia Dromaeosauridae.

facts.statement: A cladistic analysis showed that Dakotaraptor is the sister species of Dromaeosaurus.
facts.quote: Un análisis cladístico mostró que era la especie hermana de Dromaeosaurus.

facts.statement: Together with Dromaeosaurus, Dakotaraptor forms a clade with Utahraptor, within which Achillobator is an immediate lateral branch.
facts.quote: A su vez estos forman un clado con Utahraptor, clado en el cual Achillobator era una rama lateral inmediata.

facts.statement: A 2019 study suggests that Dakotaraptor is likely a member of the subfamily Unenlagiinae.
facts.quote: Un estudio publicado en 2019 por Scott Hartman, Mickey Mortimer, William R. Wahl, Dean R. Lomax, Jessica Lippincott y David M. Lovelace sugiere que Dakotaraptor probablemente es miembro de otra subfamilia de dromeosáuridos, los Unenlagiinae.

facts.statement: Wide ulnar papillae for the calaminae of large pennaceous feathers were located on the ulna in the forearm.
facts.quote: En la ulna en el antebrazo, se situaban las amplias papilas ulnares o prominencias para los cañones de las grandes plumas penáceas.

facts.statement: Adult individuals of Dakotaraptor were too heavy to fly.
facts.quote: Los individuos adultos de Dakotaraptor eran demasiado pesados para volar.

facts.statement: Possible functions for the wings include egg protection, display, intimidation, and maintaining balance while attacking prey with the killing claw.
facts.quote: Hay una variedad de posibles funciones alternativas para sus alas, incluyendo la protección de los huevos en el nido, exhibirse, la intimidación y mantener el balance mientras atacaba a una presa con la garra asesina.

facts.statement: The authors of its description considered it probable that Dakotaraptor descended from a small gliding ancestor that possessed these papillae.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, estas funciones no necesitaban de las papilas ulnares y los autores de su descripción consideraron probable que Dakotaraptor descendiera de un pequeño ancestro planeador el cual las tenía.

facts.statement: Bone histology studies showed that both the robust and gracile morphs were adults, meaning the light bone constitution was not due to a juvenile stage.
facts.quote: Un estudio de la histología de sus huesos mostró que ambos morfos eran adultos, por lo que la constitución ligera de algunos de los huesos no se debía a estar en una etapa juvenil.

facts.statement: While pathologies or individual variation could explain the difference, the simplest explanation is sexual dimorphism.
facts.quote: Las patologías o la variación individual podrían explicar la diferencia pero la explicación más sencilla es el dimorfismo sexual.

facts.statement: Dakotaraptor lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
